title: Image Captioning · Observability (DA3408 A4)
description: BLIP image-captioning app on CPU: health, throughput, latency, workload, clients and host resources (Prometheus + node_exporter).

options.content: **Read top to bottom: health → throughput → latency → workload → clients → host hardware.** Orange shaded bands mark the time a **Bulk (ZIP) job** was running, so you can line spikes in latency or CPU up with uploads. Colours are the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette, and series also differ by line style (solid / dashed / dotted), so the charts still read in greyscale print. Single mode = **blue**, Bulk mode = **orange**, errors = **vermillion**.

panels.title: ① Service health: is everything up?

options.content: Status at a glance. Blue = healthy, vermillion = needs attention; the text says the state too, so colour is never the only cue.

panels.title: Caption app · up?
panels.description: `up{job="caption-app"}`: 1 if Prometheus scraped the app's /metrics endpoint on its last attempt, 0 if it failed.

panels.title: node_exporter · up?
panels.description: `up{job="node"}`: 1 if host metrics (CPU, RAM, disk, network) are being collected.

panels.title: Model · ready?
panels.description: `caption_model_loaded`: the app sets it to 1 once the BLIP weights are in memory.

panels.title: Alerts · firing
panels.description: Number of Prometheus alert rules in the firing state (rules in prometheus/alert_rules.yml). 0 means all clear.

panels.title: Images · in range
panels.description: Successful captions (Single + Bulk) in the dashboard's time range: `increase()` of the success counter over `$__range`.

panels.title: Errors · 5 min ratio
panels.description: Failed images / all images over the last 5 minutes. Above 10 % fires the HighCaptionErrorRatio alert.

panels.title: In-flight
panels.description: `sum(caption_active_requests)`: uploads being processed now.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: `caption_active_sessions`: browser tabs connected to Streamlit.

panels.title: Model state
panels.description: `caption_app_state` (Enum): what the model is doing now: idle, single or bulk.

panels.title: App uptime
panels.description: Time since the app process started: `time() - process_start_time_seconds`.

panels.title: Alerts · pending and firing
panels.description: Every alert rule that is pending (condition true, waiting for its `for:` time) or firing. Alertmanager sends firing alerts to the alert-logger webhook.

panels.title: ② Throughput: how much work is the app doing?

options.content: Images and requests per unit time, split by mode. One Bulk request = one ZIP = many images, so Bulk shows up far more in images/s than in requests/min.

panels.title: Images captioned per second · by mode
panels.description:
Rate of successful captions (1-minute window), Single vs. Bulk, with failed images for comparison. Bulk jobs show up as plateaus that match the orange bands.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Requests per minute · by mode
panels.description:
Uploads handled per minute: a Single request is one image, a Bulk request is one ZIP.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Upload volume · bytes per second
panels.description:
Bytes received in uploads (images or ZIPs), 1-minute rate.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: ③ Latency: how fast is each caption?

options.content: Percentiles come from the **Histogram** (`caption_inference_seconds`), means from **Summary** `_sum / _count`. Log scale, because a contended CPU makes latency jump by orders of magnitude.

panels.title: Per-image inference latency · p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
Percentiles of model time per image (both modes), computed with `histogram_quantile` over 1-minute bucket rates. If p99 is far above p50, a few images (usually during Bulk jobs) are much slower than usual.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Mean latency by mode · request vs. model only
panels.description:
Solid = mean end-to-end request time (Summary `caption_request_seconds`: upload to result, a whole ZIP for Bulk). Dashed = mean model time per image (Histogram `_sum / _count`). The gap between them is decoding, queueing and UI time.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Inference latency distribution · images per bucket per minute
panels.description: Each column is one time step; each cell counts the images whose inference time fell into that latency bucket (from histogram buckets). Brighter = more images. Viridis colours are colour-blind safe and read in greyscale.

panels.title: Waiting vs. preprocessing · p95 per image
panels.description:
Queue wait = time spent waiting for the model lock while another request uses the CPU. It grows when users overlap, especially behind a Bulk job. Preprocessing = decode + RGB conversion + resize.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: ④ Workload & errors: what is being uploaded and what fails?

options.content: Size of Bulk jobs, the images inside them, and every error or skipped ZIP entry by type.

panels.title: Bulk job size · jobs by ≤ N images
panels.description: How many Bulk jobs (since app start) had up to N images: from the `caption_bulk_job_images` histogram, de-accumulated per bucket.

panels.title: Bulk progress · queue and jobs
panels.description:
Solid (left axis) = images still waiting in running Bulk jobs; it falls as batches finish. Dashed (right axis) = number of Bulk jobs in progress.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Errors per minute · by type
panels.description:
Errors by `error_type` label: corrupt images, invalid ZIPs, ZIPs with no images, model failures. A flat line at 0 is the goal.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Skipped ZIP entries per minute · by reason
panels.description:
Files inside ZIPs that were not captioned: not an image, hidden/__MACOSX, too large, over the per-job limit, or corrupt.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Image resolution · p50 / p95 megapixels
panels.description:
Size of uploaded images before resizing (`caption_image_megapixels` histogram). Large photos cost more decode time, not more model time (BLIP uses 384 px).

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Captions · length and tokens/s
panels.description:
Solid (left) = mean caption length in characters (Summary `caption_length_chars` _sum/_count). Dashed (right) = decoder tokens generated per second.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Mean upload size · by mode
panels.description:
Average size of one upload (Summary `caption_upload_size_bytes` _sum/_count): an image for Single, a whole ZIP for Bulk.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Image formats · images since start
panels.description: Successfully decoded images by file format (`caption_images_by_format_total`).

panels.title: ⑤ Clients: who is using the app?

options.content: Client metadata from custom labels: source IP, Streamlit session id (first 8 chars) and browser family. Open the app in two browsers to see two sessions.

panels.title: Requests per client · since app start
panels.description: Counter `caption_requests_total` broken down by its client labels. One row per client IP + session + browser + mode.

panels.title: Requests per minute · by client IP
panels.description:
Upload requests per minute from each source IP. Shades of blue are used because the set of clients is open-ended.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Sessions · live and new/min
panels.description:
Solid = browser sessions connected now. Dashed = new sessions started per minute, by browser family.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: ⑥ Host resources: does app load show up on the hardware? (node_exporter)

options.content: System metrics from node_exporter next to the app's own process metrics. During a Bulk job (orange band) CPU should rise with images/s, and app memory should stay flat.

panels.title: Host CPU busy % vs. images captioned per second
panels.description:
Solid (left) = % of all CPU cores busy on the host (100 − idle). Dashed (right) = images captioned per second. If the two rise and fall together, the captioning app is what loads the CPU.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: CPU cores in use · caption app vs. rest of host
panels.description:
Stacked: CPU cores used by the caption-app process (`process_cpu_seconds_total`) and by everything else on the host. The top of the stack is total busy cores.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Memory · host used vs. caption-app RSS
panels.description:
Solid = host RAM in use (MemTotal − MemAvailable). Dashed = resident memory of the caption-app process. Dotted = memory held by the BLIP weights alone.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Disk I/O · read and write throughput
panels.description:
Bytes per second read from / written to physical disks (partitions and loop devices are excluded by node_exporter).

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Network · receive and transmit
panels.description:
Bytes per second on physical interfaces (loopback, Docker bridges and veth pairs excluded). Uploads to the app show up as receive spikes.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Load average vs. CPU count
panels.description:
1- and 5-minute load averages. The dotted line is the number of CPU cores: load above it means processes are waiting for CPU.

X axis: wall-clock time (5 s samples).

panels.title: Filesystem usage · % used per mount
panels.description: Share of each real filesystem that is used. Orange from 80 %, vermillion from 90 % (the HostDiskAlmostFull alert fires below 10 % free).
